title: Bookkeeper
description:
Are you an experienced Bookkeeper looking to join a firm where modern technology, strong client relationships and continuous improvement genuinely matter?

This is an opportunity to support a varied portfolio of businesses with their day-to-day finance requirements, working as part of an established and supportive team. Your responsibilities will include:
- Processing client invoices and maintaining accurate accounting records
- Completing bank reconciliations within agreed timescales
- Managing data entry and sales and purchase ledgers
- Drafting client payment runs
- Raising sales invoices and supporting credit control
- Keeping workflow and task-management systems accurate and up to date

- Raising any risks or errors with the appropriate manager

You may already be working as a Bookkeeper within an accountancy practice, outsourced finance provider or in-house finance team.

- Strong attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy
- The ability to manage several priorities and meet deadlines
- Confidence using Microsoft Excel, Word and other everyday systems
- Experience with Xero or other cloud accounting software, or the willingness to develop it
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and improving processes
- The ability to work flexibly and supportively within a busy team

This could suit an established Bookkeeper seeking a new environment or someone who has developed a solid foundation in accounting and is ready to take the next step.

You'll be joining a respected local firm with a forward-thinking approach, a broad client base and a team that values quality, collaboration and professional development.

title: Bursary Support Administrator
description:
Bursary Support Administrator

Location: Cambridge / Huntingdon (Dual-site coverage required)

Contract Type: Temporary (8 Weeks)

Hours: Full-Time, 37 hours per week

Pay Rate: £14 - £15 per hour

About the Role

Are you an experienced administrator with strong attention to detail and a passion for supporting students?

Randstad is currently recruiting for a Bursary Support Administrator to join the Student Advice and Safeguarding team within a leading Further Education college. In this dynamic, student-facing role, you will coordinate the administration of all college bursaries, assess student applications, and ensure funding is allocated accurately to support learners throughout their educational journey.

Key Responsibilities
- Application Assessment: Evaluate incoming student bursary applications, verifying supporting documentation, and allocating financial support in accordance with college and funding guidelines.
- Student & Staff Advisory: Act as a key point of contact for bursary-related queries via email, Microsoft Teams, phone, and face-to-face drop-ins at the Student Services Hub front desk.
- Finance Collaboration: Work closely with the Finance Department to ensure timely, regular bursary disbursements throughout the term.
- Data & Systems Management: Maintain accurate, confidential, and auditable records using bespoke systems such as PayMyStudent, Promonitor, and EBS.
- Appeals & Reporting: Assist the Student Support & Safeguarding Manager by compiling documentation for bursary appeals and gathering data to track key performance indicators (KPIs).
- Information & Compliance: Help update bursary guidance across college channels, uphold equal opportunities, and ensure strict compliance with GDPR.
- General Support: Provide wider administrative cover during peak enrolment periods and participate in Open Events via a team rota.

Key RequirementsEssential:
- Qualifications: GCSEs (or equivalent) in English and Maths at Grade C/4 or above.
- Experience: Proven track record in a busy administrative role with strong customer service experience.
- Technical Skills: Proficiency with bespoke administrative software, databases, and IT packages.
- Communication & Care: Excellent written and verbal communication, with the patience and empathy required to interact with young and potentially vulnerable learners.
- Flexibility & Mobility: Willingness to split working hours between both the Cambridge and Huntingdon campuses as needed.
- Compliance: Subject to a satisfactory Enhanced DBS check (or an active DBS on the Update Service) and a 6-month probationary period.

Desirable:
- Level 3 Qualification in Business Administration.
- Prior experience working within a Further Education (FE) or Post-16 learning environment.
- Familiarity with education management systems (PayMyStudent, Promonitor, EBS).

What You'll Get in Return
- Competitive hourly rate aligned with APT & C Scale 5.
- Access to the Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS).
- The opportunity to gain valuable experience in a well-regarded educational institution.
- Supportive team environment within a vibrant Student Experience Directorate.

How to Apply

If you have the administrative skills, attention to detail, and customer focus to make an immediate impact in this 8-week placement, we want to hear from you.

Apply online today with your up-to-date CV!

description: Job description We are seeking a enthusiastic Patient Services Administrator to work across our two sites in The Red House Surgery & the Medical Centre based at Anglia Ruskin University. Flexibility is essential to cover shift patterns across our opening hours, which are 08:00 am to 18.30 pm Monday to Friday This position is part time, working 23 hours per week Monday 08:00 - 18:00 Wednesday 13:00 - 18:00 Friday 08:00 - 18:00 We strive to promote a good work life balance and have a lovely working environment. We are looking for a friendly and reliable individual to join our multi-skilled administration team. To be the main point of contact for patients, both via telephone, online and face-to-face. It will be the successful candidates job to direct patients to the most appropriate care and manage patient queries in a positive and helpful way. The successful candidate will be responsible for:- Greeting Patients and visitors Answering incoming telephone calls Booking, amend and cancelling appointments Processing Patient referrals Processing repeat prescriptions Registering patients document management coding records, liaising with external services booking interpreters dealing with test results. General administration In addition, responding to tasks from clinical and non-clinical staff liaising with external community services and emergency services Reception / admin experience would be advantageous as would previous use of SystmOne although full training will be given. The ideal candidate will be flexible, friendly, with excellent customer service and IT skills and work well within a team, whilst also able to use their own initiative. Previous NHS administration experience would be advantageous but full training will be given to the right person with scope for career development. Post Titl: Patient Services Administrator Responsible to : Practice Manager Work in a team to provide a reception / administration service to the practice always ensuring a high standard of patient care. Patient Care Dealing with patients, visitors and other health professionals either in person or on the telephone To administer the appointment booking system To answer patient enquiries with the support of other practice staff as necessary Administrative To prepare repeat prescriptions in accordance with the practice policies and protocols. Scanning of referral letters, medical reports etc directly into patients electronic notes. To prepare & process referrals using the e-referral system. To undertake all tasks associated with the day-to-day running of the computer system including the links with patient services Entering new patient registrations and updating patient information onto the database. To undertake all other administrative duties necessary to support the smooth running of the surgery and as directed by the Practice Manager. Team working Develop, apply and disseminate to all reception team own areas of knowledge and expertise Continually seek ways of improving procedures and workflows to maximise effectiveness of reception team Understanding of requirement of confidentiality at all times The practice places great emphasis on team working and aims to foster good relationships throughout the team. All staff are encouraged to attend appropriate staff meetings and take part in other activities important to practice life. Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately In the performance of the duties outlined in this job description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data Health & safety: The post-holder will implement and lead on a full range of promotion and management their own and others health and safety and infection control as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy, the practice Health & Safety Manual, and the practice Infection Control policy and published procedures. This will include (but will not be limited to): Using personal security systems within the workplace according to Practice guidelines Awareness of national standards of infection control and cleanliness and regulatory / contractual / professional requirements, and good practice guidelines Equality and diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication: The post-holder should recognize the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognize peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the implementation of services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate

title: Community Engagement Lead
description:
Community Engagement Lead

Salary: £30,000-£33,500 per annum, depending on experience

Hours: 37 hours per week, including some evening and weekend working

Contract: Permanent

Location: Hybrid, with extensive travel across Cambridgeshire, Peterborough and Norfolk

Closing date: 9.00am on 7 October 2026

Are you a natural relationship-builder who enjoys connecting with people and bringing communities together? Could you help raise awareness of unpaid carers and build partnerships that make a meaningful difference?

We are looking for an enthusiastic and engaging Community Engagement Lead to increase awareness of unpaid carers, promote the support available through Caring Together Charity and develop strong relationships across the healthcare, community, business and voluntary sectors.

About Caring Together

For over 40 years, Caring Together Charity has been supporting families who are living with an illness or disability.

Our vision is a world with no unpaid carer in crisis, isolated or struggling alone. Three in five of us will become a carer at some point in our lives, and we are here to provide emotional and practical support and advice to unpaid carers of all ages and their families.

About the role

As our Community Engagement Lead, you will be an ambassador for Caring Together Charity across Cambridgeshire, Peterborough and Norfolk.

You will build meaningful partnerships with healthcare professionals, community and voluntary organisations, local authorities, schools, faith groups and businesses. Through presentations, workshops, networking and community events, you will help more people recognise unpaid carers and understand how our services can support them.

You will also identify opportunities to reach underserved communities, support community fundraising and gather stories and insights that demonstrate the impact of our work.

This is a varied, outward-facing role requiring regular travel and some evening and weekend work. You will have the freedom to manage your own workload, develop new relationships and shape an annual programme of community outreach activity.

What you'll do

You will:
- Build and maintain relationships with GP practices, Primary Care Networks, pharmacies, hospitals, social prescribing teams and other healthcare professionals.
- Develop partnerships with community groups, voluntary organisations, local authorities, schools, faith groups and businesses.
- Represent Caring Together Charity at networking forums, community events, conferences, county shows and health and wellbeing fairs.
- Prepare and deliver engaging presentations, talks, workshops and training sessions.
- Plan and co-ordinate an annual programme of community outreach activities and events.
- Identify underserved communities and develop inclusive approaches to improve awareness and accessibility.
- Create engaging exhibition stands, information displays and resources.
- Build relationships with organisations interested in fundraising, sponsorship or partnership opportunities.
- Support community fundraising initiatives alongside fundraising colleagues.
- Gather case studies, stories, feedback and content for newsletters, social media and other communications.
- Maintain accurate records of contacts, partnerships and engagement activity on our CRM system.
- Monitor outcomes and report against agreed objectives and KPIs.
- Co-ordinate volunteers supporting community outreach and engagement activities.

About you

We are looking for someone who:
- Has experience of proactively working with a range of community partners.
- Is a natural communicator and relationship-builder, with warmth and authenticity.
- Is a confident and engaging public speaker.
- Has experience of delivering presentations and talks to different audiences.
- Can create engaging displays and represent an organisation effectively at events.
- Is highly organised and able to manage their own workload and priorities.
- Can identify and develop new partnership and engagement opportunities.
- Is comfortable using Microsoft Office, including creating PowerPoint presentations.
- Records information accurately and understands the importance of timely reporting.
- Is self-motivated, collaborative and committed to making a positive difference.
- Has a positive, practical and solutions-focused approach.
- Has a full driving licence, access to their own vehicle and the ability to travel extensively across our region.
- Can regularly work evenings and weekends when required.

Experience within healthcare, the voluntary sector or a community engagement role would be an advantage. Knowledge or personal experience of unpaid caring, experience of using Salesforce or another CRM system, and experience of supporting volunteers would also be welcomed.

Skills, attitude and experience are more important to us than specific qualifications.

What you can expect

As part of our team, you will receive:
- A salary of £30,000-£33,500, depending on experience.
- 25 days' annual leave plus bank holidays.
- The option to buy or sell annual leave in line with our policy.
- Flexible working arrangements where these can be mutually agreed.
- Time off in lieu for additional evening and weekend hours worked.
- A workplace pension in line with auto-enrolment requirements.
- The opportunity to develop meaningful partnerships and shape community engagement across our region.
- The chance to make a positive difference to unpaid carers and families across Cambridgeshire, Peterborough and Norfolk.

We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and celebrate different approaches, experiences and points of view.

Caring Together Charity is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of adults at risk and children. The successful candidate will be required to complete a Disclosure and Barring Service check appropriate to the role.

If you are ready to use your communication skills, creativity and enthusiasm to build stronger communities and help more unpaid carers access the support they need, we would love to hear from you. Apply by 9.00am on 7 October 2026.

title: Part Time Purchase Ledger Clerk
description:
Looking for a part-time finance role where your accuracy and organisation really make a difference?

We're recruiting on behalf of a well-established and growing engineering business looking to add a Purchase Ledger Clerk to its friendly finance team.

This is an ideal opportunity for someone who enjoys working with numbers, takes pride in accuracy and is looking for a part-time position offering 18 hours per week across three days. Working on-site, you'll become an integral member of the finance function, ensuring suppliers are paid accurately and on time while supporting the wider team with a variety of finance administration tasks.

The Role

As Purchase Ledger Clerk, you'll take ownership of the day-to-day purchase ledger, maintaining accurate financial records and building positive relationships with suppliers and internal stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
- Process purchase invoices accurately, including coding and VAT allocation.
- Create and maintain supplier accounts and keep supplier records up to date.
- Prepare BACS and cheque payment runs.
- Match invoices to purchase orders and delivery notes.
- Reconcile supplier statements and investigate discrepancies.
- Resolve supplier queries promptly and professionally.
- Process employee expenses and petty cash transactions.
- Support month-end and year-end activities, audits and wider finance administration.
- Work closely with the Finance Manager to ensure the smooth running of the purchase ledger function.

About You

You'll be organised, detail-oriented and enjoy working within a collaborative finance team.

Ideally, you'll have:
- At least two years' experience in a Purchase Ledger, Accounts Payable or Finance Assistant role.
- Experience working within an accounts department or accountancy practice.
- AAT studies in progress, AAT qualified, or qualified through experience.
- Strong communication skills and a proactive approach.
- Good Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel, Word and Outlook.
- SAP experience would be advantageous but is not essential.
- Excellent attention to detail and the ability to prioritise your workload effectively.

What's on Offer?
- FTC until December 2026 - with the possibility of becoming permanent
- Part-time hours (18 hours across 3 days).
- Stable, long-term opportunity within an established business.
- Supportive and friendly finance team.
- Varied role with genuine responsibility.
- Competitive salary and benefits.
